author: Caroline LeCour
title: Voters turn to new leadership in state, federal primary races to represent Connecticut - NewsBreak
text:
By Caroline LeCour ,
5 hours ago
HARTFORD, Conn. (WTNH) — Multiple challengers to long-time incumbents came out on top during Connecticut’s primary election Tuesday, as voters look for new voices in leadership.
Connecticut Election Results In New Haven, Elm City native Eli Sabin is running to represent the 92nd District in the state House of Representatives. The position has been held by Rep. Patricia Dillon, state Deputy House Majority Leader, for over three decades.
“I think what’s clear is what we’ve been doing as a Democratic Party in recent years has not been enough to deliver for families and there’s a lot more work that needs to get done,” Sabin said.
Ultimately, Dillon was unseated by Sabin despite her plethora of experience at the state Capitol. Sabin says the change doesn’t come as a surprise to him after conversations with voters, noting the race didn’t only come down to the issues, but who can bring a fresh perspective to the Democratic Party.
“Such a challenging moment that we’re in as a community here in New Haven, as a state, as a country. Throughout this campaign, we asked voters to believe in the concept of change,” Sabin added.
Also in New Haven, Wildaliz Bermudez came out on top to represent the 97th District over her competition, Assistant Attorney General Leland Moore, despite his decade of experience at the state Capitol.
The shift also reached the race for Connecticut’s 1st Congressional District, with former Hartford Mayor Luke Bronin ousting Rep. John Larson by over 12,000 votes. Larson was seeking a 15th term.
Despite running on similar issues, from the affordability crisis to housing, Bronin argues voters are looking for more than just a safe choice.
“The question isn’t how are you going to vote on a particular piece of legislation that happens to come in front of you,” Bronin said. “It’s what are you going to do to help change the political climate, to help create the conditions where more votes become possible; where bigger change becomes possible.”
Bronin’s predecessor took the loss Tuesday evening with grace and even spoke to the voter’s feelings of embracing change.
“The people in this district have spoken, and it’s time for us to come together and make sure that we all join forces,” Larson reminded.
